name: Palindrome Classifier
behavior: A 2-layer, 2-head attention-only transformer classifies whether a sequence of integers is a palindrome. Given START token followed by N integers followed by END token, the model outputs 1 (palindrome) or 0 (not palindrome) at the END position. Explain the full mechanism: how do attention heads detect (non-)palindromic structure, what do the QK and OV circuits compute, and which heads are responsible.
oracle_notes: Ablate agent-identified heads; accuracy should drop significantly on non-palindromes. Baseline accuracy ~95%+.

name: First Unique Character
behavior: A 2-layer, 3-head attention-only transformer reads a sequence of characters and at each position outputs the first non-repeating character seen so far (or '?' if none exists). The null token '?' is also used as a START token. Explain how the model tracks character repetition across positions — which heads implement which part of the algorithm, and what the QK/OV circuits compute.
oracle_notes: Ablate agent-identified heads; per-position accuracy should drop. Also check: does ablating head X break tracking of repeated chars specifically?

name: Cumulative Sum Sign Tracker
behavior: A transformer reads a sequence of integers and at each position outputs whether the running cumulative sum is positive (2), zero (1), or negative (0). Explain the full mechanism: how does the model accumulate the running sum, what circuits track sign, and which components handle the zero/boundary case.
oracle_notes: Ablate agent-identified components; per-position sign accuracy should drop. Particularly interesting: does ablation hurt the zero-detection case more than pos/neg?

name: Sorted List Classifier
behavior: A transformer reads [START, a1, ..., a10, END] and outputs 1 (sorted) or 0 (unsorted) at the END position. Explain how the model detects ordering violations: which heads compare adjacent or non-adjacent elements, what the OV circuits project onto, and whether the model is doing something clever (e.g. only checking adjacent pairs vs all pairs).
oracle_notes: Ablate agent-identified heads; accuracy on unsorted sequences (where exactly one adjacent pair is swapped) should drop most.

name: 4-Digit Addition
behavior: A 3-layer, 3-head attention-only transformer adds two 4-digit numbers given in little-endian format: [d0, d1, d2, d3, +, e0, e1, e2, e3, =, ?]. The model outputs the 4 digits of the sum. Explain the carry propagation mechanism: how the model handles carries across digit positions, which heads route information between positions, and whether the algorithm is interpretable as a clean circuit.
oracle_notes: Ablate agent-identified heads; digit-level accuracy should drop, especially for digits that require carry propagation. Construct carry-heavy examples (e.g. 9999 + 1) as adversarial tests.

name: Balanced Bracket Classifier
behavior: A 3-layer transformer classifies whether a bracket sequence is balanced. The model uses two distinct failure modes: total elevation failure (net negative depth) and negative failure (depth goes negative at some point). Explain the full circuit: which heads track running depth, how the model detects each failure mode, and what the MLP layers contribute.
oracle_notes: Ablate agent-identified components; accuracy should drop on both failure modes. A strong answer handles elevation failure and negative failure separately.
review_notes: Canonical ARENA walkthrough — known solution exists. Risk of agent regurgitating. Consider withholding the 'two failure modes' framing from the task prompt.

name: Caesar Cipher Decoding (Easy)
behavior: A transformer reads text encoded with a Caesar cipher (fixed shift applied to each character) and outputs the decoded text. Vocab: lowercase letters + space. Explain how the model identifies the shift and applies it — does it use a lookup, a linear projection, or something more compositional? Which layers/heads are responsible for shift detection vs character translation?
oracle_notes: Ablate agent-identified components; per-character decoding accuracy should drop. Extra: does ablation affect all shifts equally or specific shifts more?
review_notes: Checkpoint is self-contained but dataset generation requires downloading openwebtext-10k from HuggingFace. Need to either pre-generate and bundle a fixed test set, or patch dataset.py to use a local corpus.

name: Trigram Prediction
behavior: A transformer is trained on sequences where certain (a, b) -> c trigram rules determine the next token. Explain how the model discovers and applies trigram rules: does it use induction-head-like mechanisms, are the trigrams stored in specific heads or MLP weights, and how does the model handle positions not governed by any trigram?
oracle_notes: Ablate agent-identified components; accuracy on trigram-governed positions should drop more than non-trigram positions.
review_notes: Dataset is fully self-contained (fixed seed). Oracle framing is less crisp than others — what counts as 'finding the circuit' needs to be defined before this is ready.

name: OthelloGPT Linear Probes
behavior: A GPT trained to predict legal Othello moves develops an internal world model of the board state. Using the provided linear probe (which maps residual stream -> board state), explain which layers encode board state, whether the representation is 'mine/theirs' vs 'black/white', and what happens to the representation when the player perspective flips mid-game.
oracle_notes: Run probe at each layer; check if agent's stated peak layer matches actual peak within +/- 1.
review_notes: Probe .pth is included. OthelloGPT model itself needs download — need to identify the correct HuggingFace model ID ARENA expects.

name: Indirect Object Identification (GPT-2 Small)
behavior: GPT-2 Small correctly completes sentences like 'When Mary and John went to the store, John gave a drink to __' with 'Mary'. Reproduce the IOI circuit from Wang et al. 2022: identify name mover heads, backup name mover heads, negative name mover heads, and S-inhibition heads. Explain what each class of head computes and how they interact.
oracle_notes: Ablate agent-identified name mover heads; logit difference (P(IO) - P(S)) should drop. Compare against Wang et al. 2022 Table 1 as ground truth.
review_notes: Requires GPT-2 from HuggingFace. Well-known result — high memorization risk. Good benchmark validity but weak test of genuine reasoning. Consider a less-studied model or a corrupted/distilled variant.

name: Induction Heads in 2-Layer Transformer
behavior: A small 2-layer attention-only transformer develops induction heads: heads that implement the 'previous token + copy' pattern, enabling in-context learning. Identify which heads are induction heads vs previous-token heads, characterize their QK circuits via full OV circuit analysis, and measure their contribution via ablation on repeated-token sequences.
oracle_notes: Induction score = avg attention weight on the token after the previous occurrence of current token. Ablating induction head should reduce to near zero.
review_notes: HuggingFace model ID needs verification. Very well-known result — low oracle fidelity as a test of genuine reasoning. Probably better as a sanity-check / warm-up task than a real benchmark entry.
